newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says may take steps against DKB over scandal.
newsitem.headline: MOF says may take steps against DKB over scandal.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday the ministry may take strict measures against Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) when the bank's role in a widening racketeer payoff scandal became clear.

Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee that the Ministry of Finance (MOF) would closely watch developments in prosecutors' investigations into DKB's questionable loans to a "sokaiya" racketeer at the centre of a scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

"The impact of this case on the overall financial industry is by no means small," he said. "(The ministry) may take strict measures when the overall picture of the (prosecutors') investigation becomes clear."
On Tuesday, the Tokyo Public Prosecutors' office raided DKB in connection with their investigation into the scandal involving Nomura.
Mitsuzuka told the parliamentary committee that he regretted the prosecutors' raid on DKB.
"The raid is very regrettable," he said. "The Finance Ministry will keep a close watch on developments with the utmost interest," he said.
Kimio Yamaguchi, director-general of the ministry's Banking Bureau, told the committee that he had instructed ministry officials to examine DKB's links with the racketeer.
Not only prosecutors but also the Finance Ministry must also deal with the case appropriately, he said.
Jiji news agency reported on Wednesday that Tokyo prosecutors had raided the homes of current and former executives of DKB.
